title: The wagon wheel that runs backwards

data.source: Nyquist (1928), Shannon (1949), Itoh (1982). Computed on a steady rotor, the worked rotor of Phoenix_Egg/CORE/MATHEMATICS.md section IV, and 40 noisy runs, seeded.

prediction: A recording gives the right count exactly when the phase advances less than one half-turn between samples: for a steady rotor that is half the period, 3.1416, and for the worked rotor it is the fast half-turn, 1.2092, not half the period, 1.8138.
baseline: The sampling theorem (Nyquist 1928; Shannon 1949) and Itoh's unwrapping condition (1982).
why: The largest safe gap between samples was the fastest half-turn in both rotors, and just past it the recovered count was wrong or even negative. R2's "sampling adequacy" (ASSUMPTION; Phoenix's own check 1c saw a lost crossing) is therefore the sampling theorem in Itoh's form, and the half-turn CRR cuts at is the same half-turn the theorem is written in. CRR gives no sampling rate of its own, so nothing is added.
